title: Emotional intelligence, resilience, and perceived stress: Insights from rural healthcare professionals in India
abstract: This study examined the statistical associations among Emotional Intelligence (EI), Resilience (RS), and Perceived Stress (PSS) among 286 healthcare professionals. Partial Least Squares Structural Equation Modeling (PLS-SEM) using SmartPLS 4 was employed to assess the proposed model, which demonstrated satisfactory fit (SRMR = 0.057) and explained 64.8% of the variance in PSS ( R 2 = 0.648). Results indicated a very strong positive association between EI and RS (β = 0.990, p < 0.001). RS was negatively associated with PSS (β = −0.563, p < 0.001), and EI also showed a significant direct negative association with PSS (β = −0.426, p = 0.002). Mediation analysis revealed a significant indirect association between EI and PSS through RS (β = −0.557, p < 0.001). Overall, the findings suggest that EI and RS function as closely related psychological resources associated with lower perceived stress among healthcare professionals working in demanding rural settings.
